In the Javelin, Brian King threw over 9'0" further than before to beat Colin Clair by only 1" with Barry Townsend 3rd. Brian's magnificent effort just halted Colin's bid for a treble as he took the discus and shot, both with best distances by Belgravians so far this year.
John Martin reached his best Shot mark of 36'11" to beat Bill Couzens for 3rd spot, with Bill occupying a similar position in the Javelin behind Brian King.

Another to break new ground was Brian King , who rose to the occasion in the Club Championships with a Javelin throw of 9'0" farther than ever before, now topping that mark by a further 9'0" for 185'2" to gain 4th place.

Good marks in the sprints and field events resulted in a pleasing win against these two strong clubs. Colin Clair and John Mitchell scored a one,two in the Shot with the former going on to grab 2nd place in the Javelin from Brian King, 3rd.
The final result was not certain until the last event, the Javelin, was finished and here Brian King did his duty by beating the nearest Blackheath rival by 4 feet.

However, Field Event Captain Brian King, who upped his best last year by 20 feet to 185 feet, added still more in his first competition of the season in spite of being troubled by a bruised throwing arm.

Nick Head and field events captain Brian King make this one of our strong events and the right day could have both men over 200 ft.

Our only other winner was Brian King, who beat quite a fair field in the Javelin in very difficult throwing conditions. Overall we were probably lucky to find other teams weak and thus to finish second.
Otherwise Nick Head and Frank Glass shared the throwing events between them,with a particularly close javelin competition going to Nick ahead of Brian King.

In the field, only Brian King performed to any great effect. However, our best moment came in the medley relay, where we led all the way until the last 50 yards, where John Boardman was overhauled by Barrington of Poly, despite having run his leg in under 1:58.0.
